why: With the published sklearn defaults (alpha=1e-4, no early stopping) the per-model MLP heads memorise the training set (final training half-MSE ~0.002 on 0/1 rewards) and route below the train-selected single model. Regularisation and early stopping are therefore selected on source validation, exactly like the architecture already was.

sklearn_semantics.early_stopping_score: R2 on a random 10% of the fit rows, best weights restored

selection: per (outer split, representation, lambda): the (architecture, alpha, early_stopping) with the highest inner source-validation utility; ties -> first in the order above. Outer test outcomes are never used.
reader: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct hidden_states[21], last input token (the paper's L21)
target: per-model utility r - lambda*c (the paper's historical adaptation of the RouterBench MLP router)
llmrouterbench_lambda_note: RouterBench grid / 20 (the paper maps the benchmarks at equal lambda*c_strongest, factor ~19: 0.5<->10, 2<->38, 5<->94, 10<->189) plus the earlier LLMRouterBench points 2 and 10.
llmrouterbench_missing_policy: 278 cells (gpt-5-chat on every tau2 row) are recorded as reward 0 and cost 0, as in astra_reward_transfer_20260922_v1; missing_choice_rate is reported.
